verdict.reasoning: Patient reports dysuria and frequency for just under a week and lower abdominal pain worse with urination: "it's being going on for a few days now" then clarifies "just under a week"; "it quite hurts when I kind of pee"; "I'm going to the toilet a lot more"; "it's kind of at the bottom of my tummy ... mainly when I go to the loo, I think that's when it's worse."

She describes pink urine today: "today I noticed, um, that it was like a bit pink. The, the urine" and when asked about red blood she replies "Yeah, I think just today . Um, I think it was probably but I don't know it was pink so." This supports possible gross hematuria.

She denies back pain, fever, nausea and vomiting: back/flank pain—"does the pain move towards your back?..." "No, no, no"; nausea/vomiting—"Any other symptoms? Nausea? Vomiting?" "No, no nausea vomiting."; fevers—"Any temperatures or fevers?" "Um no, no not that I've noticed."
She reports IBS: "I think I have, um, IBS" and later doctor summarizes "apart from the IBS, is there anything else I should be aware of?"
She is on a combined oral contraceptive: "Uh yeah, uh I'm um on the pill." and then clarifies "combined pill."

She takes mebeverine for IBS: "I take, um, something for the IBS as well. Um it begins with an M..." and they confirm "was it, yeah OK." / "Yeah, yeah that's it." (mebeverine is explicitly named by doctor though partly obscured).
She reports an allergy to clindamycin: "there was an antibiotic, um, called Clindamycin mycin ." and doctor says "OK, OK, OK." and will note it.
No family history of bladder or kidney problems: "in terms of family history, any history of problems with the bladder or the kidneys?" "No, no."
She is a university student living in halls with a flatmate: "I am living in halls at the moment, uh at uni ... I'm just living with a flatmate" and later confirms she is studying at university.
She drinks socially and does not smoke: "I don't smoke. Uh ,I drink occasionally, um, kind of socially, um, with friends ."
She tried cannabis once about 1.5 weeks ago: "I smoked weed for the first time. Uh, like a week and a half ago" which matches a single recent experimentation.

Doctor’s impression is uncomplicated cystitis with hematuria: "I think it's, um, probably just a simple what we'd say a UTI or a cystitis, bladder infection" and they discuss pink/red urine earlier, supporting hematuria.
IBS is unchanged from baseline: "I usually have a bit of problems with my bowels anyway, so I don't think it's any, different, from what it usually is." This supports IBS being stable.
Clindamycin allergy is recorded: see allergy statement "called Clindamycin" and doctor responds "OK... I'll make a note of that."

Recent cannabis experimentation was discussed and counseled against: doctor says "I, I don't think it's is related..." and later "I do strongly advise you to you know, um, make it a regular habit if you can" [context clearly intended to mean avoid], and again "I would strongly recommend you, you know, to avoid if you can."

Doctor offers treatment with nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim: "we've got a choice of two antibiotics something called Trimethoprim or, Nitrofurantoin which is a three day course." This implies prescribing one of them for UTI/cystitis.
Fluid intake advice given: "make sure you're well hydrated, drink plenty of fluids."

Urine sample plan: initially "It's probably worth giving us a urine sample today as well if you can, so we can send it off to the lab" and later clarifies logistics: "I will organise uh for you to come in, and drop off a sample at one of our practices, um which we can test there and then ... and send it off to the lab."
Analgesia advice: "if you are having some pain, simple Paracetamol, um, would probably be advisable."
Plan for practice to contact her with results: regarding urine sample, doctor says "we can test there and then ... and send it off to the lab uh we can back in touch with you with the results."
Safety-netting on fever, back pain, vomiting: "Do bear in mind those symptoms I mentioned about the fever and the back pain and vomiting. If you have any of those give me a call, OK?"
Follow-up advice given: "if things still are still not getting any better next week come back and see me, and we can have another look again."
